# Discovery pipeline — FUS-enabled drug repurposing

Owner: Jeremy. Status: **scripted demo built** on `main`
(`frontend/src/components/discovery/`, `frontend/src/lib/pipeline.ts`).

Recorded 2026-11-07 from Jeremy's pitch, plus what's actually in the code.
Where the two differ, the code wins and this file says so.

---

## 1. The pitch

> The blood–brain barrier was the biggest barrier to drug delivery for ALS.
> With focused-ultrasound MRI from Sunnybrook, we can now look into new drugs
> that couldn't penetrate the BBB that can potentially reduce symptoms,
> develop a cure, or increase life expectancy.

**The move is an inversion.** Every repurposing screen for a CNS disease
treats BBB permeability as a filter and throws away what can't cross. If
MRgFUS can open the barrier focally and temporarily, that discarded set
becomes the interesting one — it has been excluded on a delivery constraint,
not on biology.

This is the strongest framing the project has had, because the thing it
proposes to search is a set nobody has had a reason to search.

### It connects to work already in this repo

`data/pipeline.json` carries a **graveyard partition**: every drug that
failed a human ALS trial, split into

- `never_arrived` — predicted barrier-negative, so it may never have reached
  the tissue at the dose that mattered, and
- `arrived_failed` — predicted barrier-positive, got there, still failed.

**`never_arrived` is, by construction, the candidate pool this pitch is
about.** A drug that failed because it never arrived is the one worth
re-asking under FUS. That partition was built for the old elimination funnel;
it turns out to be the input to the new pipeline. Nobody has to rebuild it.

> **Checked 2026-11-07 against Neo's real `pipeline.json`
> (`cursor/pipeline-graph-ui`):** same BBB model, so the sets are comparable —
> but the bucket is inflated. 21 of the 24 `never_arrived` drugs have **no BBB
> prediction** (biologics or out of domain) and were filed there by default
> (`src/merge.py:211-214`). Only ceftriaxone, pentoxifylline and pioglitazone
> are predicted BBB-negative. Say "3 predicted never-arrived, 21 we can't
> call" on stage, not "24". The bigger, honest number for this pitch is the
> funnel's: **1,593 of 3,791 approved drugs predicted BBB-negative** (plus 847
> the model declines to call). That is the FUS-unlocked pool.

---

## 2. The pipeline

Jeremy's five stages, as pitched and as coded in `STAGES`:

| # | Stage | What it does | Tools |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `analysis` | An agent reads the patient record and derives the characteristics of the ideal drug for *this* person | NCBI, ClinVar, Open Targets |
| 2 | `profiles` | The same agent runs **5× in parallel**, each producing a slightly different ideal-drug profile | — |
| 3 | `embedding` | Each profile → vector in the **DRKG** embedding space → cosine search over compounds | TransE over DRKG |
| 4 | `research` | A research agent with open web search ranks the top matches for this patient | web search |
| 5 | `report` | Cited report: each drug, its effects, and the new potential FUS gives it | — |

**Stage 3 has a gap in the pitch as worded.** "The same embedding model used
in DRKG" is TransE over *entities* — it has no vector for a sentence. A
profile only gets a DRKG vector once it is written as DRKG entities (genes,
mostly). The profiles in `PROFILES` already list target genes, so: map them
to `Gene::<Entrez>` ids, average their vectors, cosine against compound
vectors. Neo's `src/drkg.py` already loads these embeddings.

Running the profile agent five times is the part worth defending. One agent
gives you one opinion; five give you a spread, and a compound that surfaces
across several profiles is a different kind of hit from one that surfaces
once. Say that out loud in the pitch — it reads as rigour, not as padding.

### Ranking dimensions

Not just biological fit. Each candidate is scored on:

- **Cost** of the drug or treatment
- **Availability** — does it exist in this country, and what do regulations allow
- **User acceptance** — would this patient consent, how standardised is it
- **Safety** — side effects against existing conditions and current medication

Plus, in the code, the pair that carries the whole argument: **`bbbAlone`**
vs **`withFus`** per candidate ("Very low" → "Requires BBB opening";
"Low" → "Motor-cortex delivery plausible"). That column *is* the thesis. It
should be the most visually prominent thing in the report.

---

## 3. What's actually built

`runDemoPipeline` replays **fixed events on timers**. Nothing calls NCBI,
no embedding runs, no agent executes. The UI labels the run "Simulated" and
the module header says every output is illustrative.

This is the right call for a 90-second demo and it should stay — but it
means **the honest claim is "here is the system we designed", not "here is
a system that found these drugs".** The sample patient (`A-0417`, bulbar
onset, 14 months, ALSFRS 38, Toronto/OHIP, `fusEligible: true`) and its
candidates are hand-written.

A live backend only has to emit the same `PipelineEvent`s. That's a clean
seam; don't let anyone collapse it under time pressure.

---

## 4. Open questions — these need people, not agents

1. **Is this the product, or is Motus?** `main` currently ships a landing
   page and a longitudinal monitoring dashboard (speech/typing/handwriting
   vs personal baseline) *and* this discovery pipeline. They share a sidebar
   and nothing else. One demo, 90 seconds — a judge can follow one argument.
   **This is the most important open question in the repo.**
2. **What is it called?** `theme.ts`, `pipeline.ts` and `report.tsx` say
   **Addo Labs**. The landing page says **motus**. Pick one today.
3. **Does the old elimination funnel feed this?** The discovery module is
   self-contained and never reads `data/pipeline.json`. Either wire the
   graveyard in as the candidate pool (§1 — cheap, and it makes the two
   tracks one story) or retire the contract and say so.
4. **Answered → [`FUS_RESEARCH.md`](FUS_RESEARCH.md).** Was: **Can we cite the Sunnybrook FUS work accurately?** The claim rests on
   it. Get real citations for BBB opening in ALS or in neurodegeneration
   generally, and be precise about what has been shown in humans versus what
   is proposed. Mark anything unverified as unverified — a judge who knows
   the field will ask.
5. **Does FaceCheck still fit?** See `FACECHECK_SPEC.md` §7.

---

## 5. Risks worth naming before a judge does

- **Safety inverts too.** Opening the BBB for a drug also opens it for
  everything else circulating, and the drugs this unlocks were often not
  designed for CNS exposure. "It can now get in" is not "it is now safe
  once it's in." Having an answer here is a strength.
- **The ranking is the claim.** Cosine similarity in DRKG plus an LLM's
  reading is a hypothesis generator, not evidence. Frame the output as "what
  to investigate next", never as a recommendation.
- **Nothing is validated.** Same rule as FaceCheck: say so on every screen.

export type Weights = Record<Criterion, boolean>

/** Fit counts double; every other enabled criterion counts once. */
export function rank(candidates: Candidate[], weights: Weights) {
  return candidates
    .map((c) => {
      let sum = 0
      let n = 0
      for (const { key } of CRITERIA) {
        if (!weights[key]) continue
        const w = key === 'fit' ? 2 : 1
        sum += c.scores[key] * w
        n += w
      }
      return { ...c, overall: n ? Math.round(sum / n) : 0 }
    })
    .sort((a, b) => b.overall - a.overall)
}

export type PipelineEvent =
  | { type: 'stage'; stage: StageId; status: 'running' | 'done' }
  | { type: 'step'; stage: StageId; lane?: number; step: AgentStep }
  | { type: 'profile'; profile: DrugProfile }
  | { type: 'matches' }
  | { type: 'candidates' }
  | { type: 'report' }

type Timed = { at: number; event: PipelineEvent }

/** What the analysis agent is told about the uploaded case PDF. */
export type CaseInput = { name: string; pages: number; words: number; excerpt: string } | null

function script(p: Patient, caseInput: CaseInput): Timed[] {

  let t = 0

}`, 700)

“${caseInput.excerpt}…”`, 900)
  }
  step('analysis', 'thinking', 'Reading patient record', `${p.label}: ${p.age}${p.sex}, ${p.onset.toLowerCase()}, ${p.monthsSinceDx} months from diagnosis. ALSFRS-R ${p.alsfrs}/48, slope ${p.slope} pts/month, FVC ${p.fvc}%. On ${p.medications.join(', ')}.`, 900)
  step('analysis', 'tool_call', 'ncbi.gene_lookup', '{\n  "genes": ["SOD1", "C9orf72", "FUS", "TARDBP"],\n  "organism": "Homo sapiens"\n}', 1100)
  step('analysis', 'tool_result', 'NCBI Gene — result', 'Retrieved gene records and ALS-associated variant summaries for 4 genes.', 1100)
  step('analysis', 'tool_call', 'clinvar.match_patient_variants', '{\n  "panel": "ALS core",\n  "patient_result": "negative"\n}', 800)

  at(300, { type: 'stage', stage: 'analysis', status: 'done' })

  // 2 — five profile agents, interleaved
  at(200, { type: 'stage', stage: 'profiles', status: 'running' })
  const base = t
  PROFILES.forEach((prof, lane) => {
    const s = base + lane * 350
    out.push({ at: s + 400, event: { type: 'step', stage: 'profiles', lane, step: { type: 'thinking', label: `Agent ${lane + 1}: framing hypothesis`, content: prof.hypothesis } } })
    out.push({ at: s + 1500, event: { type: 'step', stage: 'profiles', lane, step: { type: 'tool_call', label: `Agent ${lane + 1}: opentargets.associations`, content: `{\n  "disease": "amyotrophic lateral sclerosis",\n  "targets": ${JSON.stringify(prof.targets)}\n}` } } })

  step('research', 'tool_result', 'Search — result', 'Exploratory ALS studies only; no phase 3.', 1000)
  step('research', 'tool_call', 'interactions.check', `{\n  "candidates": ["Tocilizumab", "Anakinra", "Mecasermin", "Ravulizumab"],\n  "current": ${JSON.stringify(p.medications)},\n  "conditions": ${JSON.stringify(p.comorbidities)}\n}`, 900)

  step('research', 'tool_call', 'web.search', `{ "query": "availability in Canada: tocilizumab, anakinra, ravulizumab, mecasermin" }`, 800)
  step('research', 'tool_result', 'Search — result', 'Three of four marketed in Canada for other indications; mecasermin may need the Special Access Programme.', 1000)
  step('research', 'output', 'Ranking', 'Scored on mechanistic fit (×2), safety & interactions, cost, availability & regulation, and patient acceptance.', 700)

  step('report', 'output', 'Report compiled', '4 ranked candidates, 4 exclusions, 7 references.', 1100)
  at(300, { type: 'report' })

/** The scripted events of one stage, with times relative to the stage's start. */
function stageEvents(patient: Patient, caseInput: CaseInput, stage: StageId): Timed[] {
  let current: StageId | null = null
  const mine: Timed[] = []
  for (const t of script(patient, caseInput)) {
    if (t.event.type === 'stage' && t.event.status === 'running') current = t.event.stage
    if (current === stage) mine.push(t)
  }
  const t0 = mine[0]?.at ?? 0
  return mine.map((t) => ({ at: t.at - t0 + 150, event: t.event }))
}

/**
 * Replays ONE stage of the scripted run; the pipeline waits for the user
 * before the next. Returns `{ cancel, skip }`; `skip` finishes the stage now.
 */
export function runDemoStage(patient: Patient, caseInput: CaseInput, stage: StageId, emit: (e: PipelineEvent) => void, onDone: () => void) {
  const events = stageEvents(patient, caseInput, stage)
  let i = 0
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
  const start = performance.now()
  const tick = () => {
    const now = performance.now() - start
    while (i < events.length && events[i].at <= now) emit(events[i++].event)
    if (i >= events.length) return onDone()
    timer = setTimeout(tick, Math.max(0, events[i].at - now))
  }
  timer = setTimeout(tick, 0)
  return {
    cancel: () => clearTimeout(timer),
    skip: () => {
      clearTimeout(timer)
      while (i < events.length) emit(events[i++].event)
      onDone()
    },
  }
}

"""DRKG loading, and the one piece of knowledge everything downstream depends on:
which node and which relation actually represent "treats ALS".

Do not guess the ALS node. DRKG entity ids carry no names, so grepping the entity
list for "amyotrophic" returns nothing - you have to grep for the ontology ids and
then count the edges. Run this module to redo that check from scratch:

    python -m src.drkg

It prints the report and writes artifacts/als_node.json.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import json
import subprocess
import sys
import tarfile
from typing import Iterator

import numpy as np

from src.paths import ARTIFACTS, RAW, ensure_dirs

DRKG_URL = "https://dgl-data.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/dataset/DRKG/drkg.tar.gz"

TRIPLES = RAW / "drkg.tsv"
EMBED_DIR = RAW / "embed"
ENTITIES_TSV = EMBED_DIR / "entities.tsv"
RELATIONS_TSV = EMBED_DIR / "relations.tsv"
ENTITY_EMB = EMBED_DIR / "DRKG_TransE_l2_entity.npy"
RELATION_EMB = EMBED_DIR / "DRKG_TransE_l2_relation.npy"

# Confirmed by edge count, not by assumption. See module docstring and
# artifacts/als_node.json. MeSH D000690 is amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
ALS_NODE = "Disease::MESH:D000690"

# Candidates checked when resolving the ALS node. DOID:332 is also ALS, but it is a
# near-orphan in DRKG; D016472 is motor neuron disease, the parent term.
ALS_CANDIDATES = [
    "Disease::MESH:D000690",
    "Disease::DOID:332",
    "Disease::OMIM:105400",
    "Disease::MESH:D016472",
]

# The three relations DRKG uses for "a compound treats a disease". They come from
# different sources and - critically - they do not share a disease namespace.
TREATS_RELATIONS = [
    "DRUGBANK::treats::Compound:Disease",
    "GNBR::T::Compound:Disease",
    "Hetionet::CtD::Compound:Disease",
]

# The relation we score the missing edge with. GNBR::T carries 55 of the 57 existing
# treats edges on the ALS node, so it is the one the embedding actually learned.
SCORING_RELATION = "GNBR::T::Compound:Disease"


def download() -> None:
    """Fetch and unpack drkg.tar.gz if it is not already on disk.

    The tarball includes the pretrained TransE_l2 embeddings, so this is the only
    download component A needs.
    """
    ensure_dirs()
    if TRIPLES.exists() and ENTITY_EMB.exists():
        return
    archive = RAW / "drkg.tar.gz"
    if not archive.exists():
        print(f"downloading {DRKG_URL} (~207 MB)", file=sys.stderr)
        subprocess.run(["curl", "-sS", "-L", "-o", str(archive), DRKG_URL], check=True)
    print("unpacking", file=sys.stderr)
    with tarfile.open(archive) as tf:
        tf.extractall(RAW)


def load_entity_index() -> dict[str, int]:
    """entity name -> row in the entity embedding matrix."""
    out: dict[str, int] = {}
    with ENTITIES_TSV.open() as fh:
        for line in fh:
            name, idx = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
            out[name] = int(idx)
    return out


def load_relation_index() -> dict[str, int]:
    out: dict[str, int] = {}
    with RELATIONS_TSV.open() as fh:
        for line in fh:
            name, idx = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
            out[name] = int(idx)
    return out


def load_embeddings() -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """(entity, relation) embedding matrices, memory-mapped.

    Pretrained TransE_l2, 400 dimensions, 97,238 entities and 107 relations. We do not
    train our own; that is the first thing on the cut list.
    """
    return (
        np.load(ENTITY_EMB, mmap_mode="r"),
        np.load(RELATION_EMB, mmap_mode="r"),
    )


def iter_triples() -> Iterator[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """All 5,874,261 head/relation/tail triples."""
    with TRIPLES.open() as fh:
        for line in fh:
            h, r, t = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
            yield h, r, t


def compound_nodes(entity_index: dict[str, int] | None = None) -> list[str]:
    idx = entity_index or load_entity_index()
    return [name for name in idx if name.startswith("Compound::")]


def resolve_als_node() -> dict:
    """Count every edge on each ALS-candidate node, and report which relations and
    which disease namespaces the treats edges actually use.

    This is the gotcha the spec warns about, done as a measurement.
    """
    download()
    entity_index = load_entity_index()

    edges: dict[str, collections.Counter] = {c: collections.Counter() for c in ALS_CANDIDATES}
    treats_namespaces: dict[str, collections.Counter] = {
        r: collections.Counter() for r in TREATS_RELATIONS
    }
    treats_edges: dict[str, list[str]] = {c: [] for c in ALS_CANDIDATES}

    candidates = set(ALS_CANDIDATES)
    treats = set(TREATS_RELATIONS)
    for head, rel, tail in iter_triples():
        if rel in treats:
            namespace = tail.split("::", 1)[1].split(":", 1)[0]
            treats_namespaces[rel][namespace] += 1
        for node in (head, tail):
            if node in candidates:
                edges[node][rel] += 1
                if rel in treats:
                    treats_edges[node].append(f"{head} -[{rel}]-> {tail}")

    report = {
        "resolved_als_node": ALS_NODE,
        "scoring_relation": SCORING_RELATION,
        "candidates": [
            {
                "node": c,
                "in_entity_index": c in entity_index,
                "embedding_row": entity_index.get(c),
                "total_edges": sum(edges[c].values()),
                "treats_edges": sum(edges[c][r] for r in TREATS_RELATIONS),
                "edges_by_relation": dict(edges[c].most_common()),
                "treats_edge_examples": treats_edges[c][:5],
            }
            for c in ALS_CANDIDATES
        ],
        "treats_relation_disease_namespaces": {
            r: dict(treats_namespaces[r].most_common()) for r in TREATS_RELATIONS
        },
    }
    return report


def main() -> int:
    report = resolve_als_node()
    ensure_dirs()
    out = ARTIFACTS / "als_node.json"
    out.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")

    print("ALS node candidates in DRKG")
    print(f"{'node':28} {'in index':>9} {'edges':>7} {'treats':>7}")
    for c in report["candidates"]:
        print(
            f"{c['node']:28} {str(c['in_entity_index']):>9} "
            f"{c['total_edges']:>7} {c['treats_edges']:>7}"
        )
    print()
    print("disease namespace used by each treats relation")
    for rel, namespaces in report["treats_relation_disease_namespaces"].items():
        print(f"  {rel:42} {namespaces}")
    print()
    print(f"resolved: {report['resolved_als_node']}  scoring with {report['scoring_relation']}")
    print(f"wrote {out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Component A. Score every compound for the missing Compound-treats-ALS edge, and
produce a short typed path to ALS as the receipt the UI displays.

    python -m src.kg_rank

Writes data/kg_scores.json.

Method
------
Pretrained DRKG TransE_l2 embeddings, 400 dimensions. We do not train our own model;
that is the first item on the cut list and the pretrained vectors give a ranked list in
seconds.

TransE embeds a triple so that head + relation ~= tail, so the plausibility of the
missing edge is the negative distance between where the compound lands after the
relation translation and where ALS actually sits:

    score(c) = gamma - || e_c + e_treats - e_ALS ||_2

gamma = 12.0, the margin DGL-KE used to train these vectors. It is a constant, so it
shifts every score equally and changes no ranking; it is kept only so the numbers read
on the same scale as the published DRKG repurposing example.

Honesty note that belongs on the judging slide
----------------------------------------------
Riluzole (DB00740) and edaravone (DB12243) already have treats edges to the ALS node in
DRKG, so they were in the data these embeddings were fit on. Their ranks are a sanity
check that the scoring function is wired up correctly, not a held-out evaluation. The
module labels them `in_training_graph: true` and reports an additional rank computed over
compounds that have no existing ALS treats edge, which is the honest comparison.

Paths
-----
`data/kg_scores.json` carries a 2-3 hop typed path to ALS for the top 100, found by BFS
over a relation-filtered subgraph.

The spec asks for drug -> target gene -> pathway -> ALS. **That path does not exist in
DRKG**: there are 84,372 Gene-Pathway edges but zero Pathway-Disease edges, so a pathway
can never be the last hop before ALS. The reachable shapes, in the order we prefer them:

1. compound -> gene -> ALS                     (2 hops, gene is an ALS-associated gene)
2. compound -> gene -> gene -> ALS             (3 hops, via a gene-gene interaction)
3. compound -> gene -> pathway -> gene -> ALS  (4 hops, the pathway-mediated receipt)

Shape 3 is emitted only when 1 and 2 fail, because DRKG pathway nodes are Pathway Commons
`PC7_*` ids with no name available offline - fine as structure, poor as a UI label.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import gzip
import json
import sys
from typing import Iterable

import networkx as nx
import numpy as np

from src import crosswalk, drkg
from src.paths import DATA, KG_SCORES_JSON, RAW, ensure_dirs

GAMMA = 12.0
TOP_N_PATHS = 100
MAX_HOPS = 4

GENE_INFO = RAW / "Homo_sapiens.gene_info.gz"

POSITIVE_CONTROLS = {"Compound::DB00740": "riluzole", "Compound::DB12243": "edaravone"}

# Compound -> Gene. "This drug does something to this gene product."
COMPOUND_GENE = {
    "DRUGBANK::target::Compound:Gene": "targets",
    "DRUGBANK::carrier::Compound:Gene": "is_carried_by",
    "DRUGBANK::transporter::Compound:Gene": "is_transported_by",
    "Hetionet::CbG::Compound:Gene": "binds",
    "Hetionet::CuG::Compound:Gene": "upregulates",
    "Hetionet::CdG::Compound:Gene": "downregulates",
    "GNBR::B::Compound:Gene": "binds",
    "GNBR::E::Compound:Gene": "affects_expression_of",
    "GNBR::N::Compound:Gene": "inhibits",
    "GNBR::A+::Compound:Gene": "agonises",
    "GNBR::A-::Compound:Gene": "antagonises",
    "bioarx::DrugHumGen:Compound:Gene": "targets",
}

# Gene -> Disease, in whichever direction DRKG stores it.
GENE_DISEASE = {
    "Hetionet::DaG::Disease:Gene": "associated_with",
    "Hetionet::DuG::Disease:Gene": "upregulated_in",
    "Hetionet::DdG::Disease:Gene": "downregulated_in",
    "GNBR::L::Gene:Disease": "implicated_in",
    "GNBR::J::Gene:Disease": "linked_to",
    "GNBR::U::Gene:Disease": "causal_in",
    "GNBR::Te::Gene:Disease": "treatment_target_in",
    "GNBR::Md::Gene:Disease": "biomarker_of",
    "GNBR::X::Gene:Disease": "overexpressed_in",
    "GNBR::Y::Gene:Disease": "polymorphism_in",
}

# Gene -> Gene. Curated and physical interactions only; the four STRING::OTHER-style
# buckets are too promiscuous to be a receipt a clinician would accept.
GENE_GENE = {
    "Hetionet::GiG::Gene:Gene": "interacts_with",
    "Hetionet::Gr>G::Gene:Gene": "regulates",
    "Hetionet::GcG::Gene:Gene": "covaries_with",
    "STRING::BINDING::Gene:Gene": "binds",
    "STRING::ACTIVATION::Gene:Gene": "activates",
    "STRING::INHIBITION::Gene:Gene": "inhibits",
    "GNBR::Rg::Gene:Gene": "regulates",
    "GNBR::B::Gene:Gene": "binds",
}

GENE_PATHWAY = {"Hetionet::GpPW::Gene:Pathway": "participates_in"}

# Not every gene-disease edge is worth showing a clinician. Hetionet's DaG/DuG/DdG are
# curated associations and GNBR::U/Te are causal or therapeutic-target statements; the
# rest are literature co-occurrence, which is why an untiered BFS routes half the top 100
# through CRP. Tier 1 is tried first, and only if it finds nothing do we accept tier 2.
STRONG_GENE_DISEASE = {
    "Hetionet::DaG::Disease:Gene",
    "Hetionet::DuG::Disease:Gene",
    "Hetionet::DdG::Disease:Gene",
    "GNBR::U::Gene:Disease",
    "GNBR::Te::Gene:Disease",
}

ALLOWED = {**COMPOUND_GENE, **GENE_DISEASE, **GENE_GENE, **GENE_PATHWAY}


def load_gene_symbols() -> dict[str, str]:
    """DRKG Gene nodes are Entrez ids. Receipts need symbols, so map them."""
    if not GENE_INFO.exists():
        return {}
    symbols: dict[str, str] = {}
    with gzip.open(GENE_INFO, "rt") as fh:
        next(fh, None)
        for line in fh:
            parts = line.split("\t", 3)
            if len(parts) > 2:
                symbols[parts[1]] = parts[2]
    return symbols


def node_label(node: str, symbols: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    kind, _, ident = node.partition("::")
    if kind == "Gene":
        return symbols.get(ident, f"Gene {ident}")
    if kind == "Disease" and node == drkg.ALS_NODE:
        return "Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis"
    if kind == "Pathway":
        return f"Pathway {ident}"
    return ident


def score_compounds(
    compound_nodes: Iterable[str],
    entity_index: dict[str, int],
    relation_index: dict[str, int],
) -> dict[str, dict[str, float]]:
    """TransE score for (compound, treats, ALS) under each treats relation."""
    entity_emb, relation_emb = drkg.load_embeddings()
    als = np.asarray(entity_emb[entity_index[drkg.ALS_NODE]], dtype=np.float32)

    nodes = [c for c in compound_nodes if c in entity_index]
    rows = np.asarray([entity_index[c] for c in nodes])
    heads = np.asarray(entity_emb[rows], dtype=np.float32)

    scores: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {c: {} for c in nodes}
    for relation in drkg.TREATS_RELATIONS:
        rel = np.asarray(relation_emb[relation_index[relation]], dtype=np.float32)
        distance = np.linalg.norm(heads + rel - als, axis=1)
        values = GAMMA - distance
        for node, value in zip(nodes, values):
            scores[node][relation] = float(value)
    return scores


def build_path_graph() -> nx.DiGraph:
    """Relation-filtered directed graph for the receipt BFS.

    Edges are oriented in the direction a receipt reads - compound to gene, gene to
    disease - which is sometimes the reverse of how DRKG stores them (Hetionet writes
    Disease:Gene). Gene-gene edges go both ways because the interaction is symmetric.
    """
    graph = nx.DiGraph()
    for head, relation, tail in drkg.iter_triples():
        label = ALLOWED.get(relation)
        if label is None:
            continue
        if relation.endswith("Disease:Gene"):
            head, tail = tail, head  # store gene -> disease
        if graph.has_edge(head, tail):
            continue
        graph.add_edge(head, tail, rel=label, source=relation)
        if relation in GENE_GENE and not graph.has_edge(tail, head):
            graph.add_edge(tail, head, rel=label, source=relation)
    return graph


def find_path(
    graph: nx.DiGraph, compound: str, symbols: dict[str, str], compound_name: str | None = None
) -> list[dict[str, str]] | None:
    """Shortest allowed path from a compound to the ALS node, as UI-ready hops.

    BFS over three passes, in decreasing strength of claim: curated gene-disease edges
    without pathways, then curated edges with pathways, then any allowed edge. A receipt
    that lands on a curated ALS gene is worth more than a shorter one that lands on a
    literature co-occurrence, so strength is preferred over length.
    """
    if compound not in graph or drkg.ALS_NODE not in graph:
        return None

    for strong_only, allow_pathways in ((True, False), (True, True), (False, True)):
        queue = collections.deque([(compound, [compound])])
        seen = {compound}
        while queue:
            node, trail = queue.popleft()
            if len(trail) > MAX_HOPS:
                continue
            for nxt in graph.successors(node):
                if nxt in seen:
                    continue
                if nxt == drkg.ALS_NODE:
                    if strong_only and graph[node][nxt]["source"] not in STRONG_GENE_DISEASE:
                        continue
                    full = trail + [nxt]
                    labels = [node_label(n, symbols) for n in full]
                    if compound_name:
                        labels[0] = compound_name
                    return [
                        {"from": labels[i], "rel": graph[a][b]["rel"], "to": labels[i + 1]}
                        for i, (a, b) in enumerate(zip(full, full[1:]))
                    ]
                if nxt.startswith("Pathway::") and not allow_pathways:
                    continue
                if len(trail) + 1 > MAX_HOPS:
                    continue
                seen.add(nxt)
                queue.append((nxt, trail + [nxt]))
    return None


def existing_als_treats_edges() -> set[str]:
    """Compounds that already have a treats edge to ALS, i.e. not missing-link
    predictions at all. Needed to report an honest rank for the positive controls."""
    treats = set(drkg.TREATS_RELATIONS)
    als_nodes = {drkg.ALS_NODE, "Disease::DOID:332"}
    return {
        head
        for head, relation, tail in drkg.iter_triples()
        if relation in treats and tail in als_nodes
    }


def run() -> dict:
    drkg.download()
    entity_index = drkg.load_entity_index()
    relation_index = drkg.load_relation_index()
    symbols = load_gene_symbols()

    # The candidate universe: approved substances that carry a DRKG compound node,
    # joined on an RDKit InChIKey rather than a name. Falls back to every DRKG compound
    # node if the crosswalk has not been built yet, so this module never hard-blocks.
    universe: dict[str, dict] = {}
    try:
        for row in crosswalk.load():
            for node in filter(None, row["drkg_ids"].split("|")):
                universe.setdefault(
                    node,
                    {
                        "inchikey": row["inchikey"],
                        "name": row["drugcentral_name"],
                        "smiles": row["smiles"],
                        "drugcentral_id": row["drugcentral_id"],
                    },
                )
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print("no crosswalk yet; scoring every DRKG compound node", file=sys.stderr)

    all_compounds = drkg.compound_nodes(entity_index)
    scores = score_compounds(all_compounds, entity_index, relation_index)
    already_treats = existing_als_treats_edges()

    primary = drkg.SCORING_RELATION
    ranked_all = sorted(scores, key=lambda c: -scores[c][primary])
    rank_all = {c: i + 1 for i, c in enumerate(ranked_all)}

    in_universe = [c for c in ranked_all if c in universe] if universe else ranked_all
    rank_universe = {c: i + 1 for i, c in enumerate(in_universe)}

    # The held-out view: rank among compounds with no existing ALS treats edge, so a
    # drug that was in the training graph does not flatter itself.
    novel = [c for c in in_universe if c not in already_treats]
    rank_novel = {c: i + 1 for i, c in enumerate(novel)}

    graph = build_path_graph()

    compounds = []
    for node in in_universe:
        meta = universe.get(node, {})
        entry = {
            "drkg_id": node,
            "drugbank_id": node.split("::", 1)[1] if node.startswith("Compound::DB") else None,
            "inchikey": meta.get("inchikey"),
            "name": meta.get("name") or POSITIVE_CONTROLS.get(node) or node.split("::", 1)[1],
            "smiles": meta.get("smiles"),
            "score": round(scores[node][primary], 4),
            "rank": rank_universe[node],
            "rank_all_compounds": rank_all[node],
            "rank_excluding_known_als_drugs": rank_novel.get(node),
            "in_training_graph": node in already_treats,
            "scores_by_relation": {
                relation: round(scores[node][relation], 4) for relation in drkg.TREATS_RELATIONS
            },
            "path": None,
        }
        compounds.append(entry)

    for entry in compounds[:TOP_N_PATHS]:
        entry["path"] = find_path(graph, entry["drkg_id"], symbols, entry["name"])

    with_paths = sum(1 for e in compounds[:TOP_N_PATHS] if e["path"])
    controls = {}
    for node, name in POSITIVE_CONTROLS.items():
        entry = next((e for e in compounds if e["drkg_id"] == node), None)
        controls[name] = (
            {
                "drkg_id": node,
                "score": entry["score"],
                "rank": entry["rank"],
                "rank_all_compounds": entry["rank_all_compounds"],
                "in_training_graph": entry["in_training_graph"],
                "universe_size": len(in_universe),
            }
            if entry
            else None
        )

    doc = {
        "meta": {
            "als_node": drkg.ALS_NODE,
            "scoring_relation": primary,
            "model": "DRKG pretrained TransE_l2, 400d (not retrained)",
            "score_definition": "gamma - L2(head + relation - tail), gamma = 12.0",
            "gamma": GAMMA,
            "universe_size": len(in_universe),
            "all_drkg_compound_nodes": len(scores),
            "compounds_with_existing_als_treats_edge": len(
                [c for c in in_universe if c in already_treats]
            ),
            "paths_requested": TOP_N_PATHS,
            "paths_found": with_paths,
            "max_hops": MAX_HOPS,
        },
        "validation": {
            "positive_controls": controls,
            "caveat": (
                "Riluzole and edaravone already have treats edges to "
                f"{drkg.ALS_NODE} in DRKG, so these embeddings saw them. Their ranks "

# DRKG queries for ALS research

From the BioHacks root, run with Python 3.9+ and NumPy:

```sh
python3 backend/query-generation/run.py --top-k 100
```

The first run downloads the official DRKG TransE-L2 release and two terminology tables. The loader checks SHA-256 hashes of the graph, ID mappings, glossary, matrices and terminology. Subsequent runs reuse those files. Internet access refreshes the documentary checks on provisional leaders. `--offline` uses the local data and adjudicated records. No credentials are required. [DRKG release](https://github.com/gnn4dr/DRKG) · [MeSH descriptors](https://www.nlm.nih.gov/databases/download/mesh.html) · [Hetionet nodes](https://github.com/hetio/hetionet/tree/main/hetnet/tsv)

Open `reports/alex-gated-research/summary.md` for the shortlist, individual dossiers and one worked query per agent. `reports/alex-gated.json` holds every computed distance, trial record, eligibility decision, review and rank. The generated files and downloaded inputs stay local. [Saved Alex run](snapshots/alex-gated-research/summary.md)

## Eligibility before scoring

The versioned `examples/als-study-cache.json` contains adjudicated primary studies, tested ingredient aliases, dosage forms, co-treatments, populations, study status, clinical results and sources. A study must document administration in a human ALS interventional cohort. Positive, negative, inconclusive and unreported outcomes can all meet the exposure criterion. Results are specific to the tested population, endpoint and formulation.

The gate normalizes case, punctuation and explicit aliases. It checks each identified ingredient of a combination separately. It never strips salts, infers an ingredient from a class or transfers a trial to a different preparation. Each reviewed alias has a canonical DrugBank ID. Missing evidence means testing status is unknown. This is a curated evidence snapshot with bounded coverage. To extend it, add an exact ingredient identity and a qualifying administration record with a primary citation. Use `--trials` to select a different snapshot.

The workflow intersects that evidence with canonical IDs in the frozen release, then separates established ALS comparators and applies the patient-specific exclusions. All five concurrent agents, the strict intersection and the fallback receive the same immutable investigational pool. Neither trial results nor eligibility queries consume a DRKG distance.

## From record to query

`--profile` takes a case ID, a source URL, short source quotations in `facts` and optional source locations in `pointers`. The structured fields cover diagnosis, genotype, current therapy, respiratory function, weight, muscle, swallowing, hand function and other symptoms. The example quotes the project's source record. Anchor IDs are derived at runtime. [Source case](https://github.com/penguinyogurt/BioHacks-2026/blob/da0eb26f5e774491ad5b9502aa5d110168c829de/data/pipeline.json)

Terms resolve through MeSH descriptor names and entry terms, Hetionet gene and compound names, and reviewed ingredient aliases. All hits must exist in the frozen entity mapping. The resolver uses longest unique term matches and withholds negated or uncertain text. Coughing while drinking can suggest dysphagia for retrieval. The output labels this as a hypothesis. Numeric findings without an attributable mapping stay in the record for review.

| Agent | How it selects anchors and establishes support |
|---|---|
| Disease / indications | Resolve the diagnosis to MeSH. Reverse observed compound–disease treatment predicates. A supported drug has a corresponding typed edge. |
| Genes / targets | Ground an explicit gene if provided. Also traverse typed disease–gene association, causal mutation, course-modifying mutation and pathogenesis edges from the diagnosis. Keep every resulting gene with a target or binding relation. The chart need not establish a patient's genotype to explore disease-level biology. |
| Safety / interactions / class | Resolve current medication, then translate through its observed incoming and outgoing drug-interaction predicates. A suitability rank also requires documentary review and no unresolved exact-pair interaction edge. Preserve chart observations for conditional review. |
| Pathways / processes | Traverse the grounded genes into GO biological processes. Choose up to five by `linked_genes² / all_genes_in_process`, breaking ties by linked-gene count then process ID. This balances specificity and breadth before seeing drug scores. Project back through gene participation and compound target/binding. Retain compound–gene–process witnesses. |
| Symptoms / function | Resolve affirmative observations or labeled proxies and reverse observed treatment predicates. A numeric distance can exist even if no tested ingredient has the required supporting edge. |

Every translation uses the original 400-dimensional arrays. For an observed triple `(drug, r, target)`, use `q = e[target] − r`. For `(anchor, r, drug)`, use `q = e[anchor] + r`. Multi-hop paths add one signed relation per traversal. Each constructed query scores every eligible compound with Euclidean distance. The JSON records the quotation, source pointer, grounded entity IDs, derivation edges, relation names and row indices, directions, formula, scores and winning witness.

Multiple anchors denote alternative mechanistic hypotheses. A positive agent takes each drug's **smallest supported distance** and sorts ascending. This preserves one inspectable path and avoids averaging unrelated anchors into an unsupported vector. For safety, the closest risk query represents the strongest modeled concern. Only independently reviewed drugs receive a safety rank, ordered by that minimum distance descending. The model makes no safety inference from an absent edge or a large distance. It assumes adequate local delivery and uses no passive BBB feature.

## Strict ranking and fallback

First intersect all five supported top-100 lists. A missing list causes an explicit abstention. With five populated lists, a strict survivor's mean rank, worst rank and canonical ID determine its position. An empty strict result preserves its status and invokes a separately labeled research fallback.

The fallback evaluates the full eligible pool. Entry requires a cited disease, target or pathway query and supporting graph witness. Each supported category contributes

```text
(category weight / sum of all five weights) × (offset + 1) / (offset + rank) × coverage^exponent
```

Coverage is the fraction of the five weights carrying evidence. Missing categories contribute zero. The prespecified weights are 0.36 disease, 0.26 genes, 0.13 safety, 0.20 pathways and 0.05 symptoms. Offset is 10 and the default coverage exponent is zero. Use `--policy` to change these settings. A case-matched hard veto overrides all scores. A documented lesser concern costs 0.04 once. Negative clinical outcomes are reported explicitly. The resulting graph score is a research retrieval score and has no calibrated clinical meaning.

Provisional leaders receive a source review against the case, directed medication-pair graph checks and targeted Europe PMC searches. Search hits alone cannot adjudicate an interaction. Labels and primary studies are scoped to the reviewed formulation. `--review` sets the original exclusion screen and `--leader-review` selects case-matched adjudications. After each veto or deduction, the workflow examines challengers until their unpenalized score is strictly below the fifth accepted score, handling ties by canonical ID. It returns fewer than five if necessary. The output records changes, unresolved evidence, cost, Canadian availability, regulatory status and patient acceptance separately.

## Alex run

Of 10,551 canonical graph IDs, 19 had verified human ALS exposure in this cache. Alex's current riluzole and the established comparator edaravone were separated. Mexiletine and gabapentin met the original case exclusion screen. Tofersen had study evidence and no compound row in this release. The common investigational pool contained 15 IDs. The supported category counts were 9, 4, 1, 8 and 0. The symptoms agent grounded the swallowing observation but found no eligible treatment edge. Twelve IDs qualified for provisional fusion and five were returned. All five have unresolved safety. Minocycline's randomized trial documented faster functional decline. [Primary trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17980667/)

"""Typed, read-only snapshot of the official TransE-L2 release."""
from functools import lru_cache
import csv
import hashlib
import json
import subprocess
import tarfile
import shutil
from array import array
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
import numpy as np

URL = "https://dgl-data.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/dataset/DRKG/drkg.tar.gz"
SHA = "00a8154a35bda496d0fdfe0d76b058bf4bd3dd11f69d0ec00c3559523608b930"
FILES = ["drkg.tsv","relation_glossary.tsv","embed/entities.tsv","embed/relations.tsv",
         "embed/DRKG_TransE_l2_entity.npy","embed/DRKG_TransE_l2_relation.npy"]


def download(root):
    if all((root/f).is_file() for f in FILES):
        return
    root.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    with TemporaryDirectory(dir=root) as work:
        work=Path(work)
        archive=work/"archive"
        subprocess.run(["curl","-fLsS","--retry","2",URL,"-o",str(archive)],check=True)
        digest=hashlib.sha256()
        with archive.open("rb") as f:
            for chunk in iter(lambda:f.read(1<<20),b""): digest.update(chunk)
        if digest.hexdigest()!=SHA: raise ValueError("DRKG archive checksum mismatch")
        with tarfile.open(archive) as tar:
            members={m.name.removeprefix("./"):m for m in tar if m.isfile()}
            for name in FILES:
                dest=work/name
                dest.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
                with dest.open("wb") as f: shutil.copyfileobj(tar.extractfile(members[name]),f)
        for name in FILES:
            (root/name).parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
            (work/name).replace(root/name)


def mapping(path):
    result={}
    with path.open() as f:
        for name,idx in csv.reader(f,delimiter="\t"):
            if name in result: raise ValueError(f"Duplicate identifier in {path}")
            result[name]=int(idx)
    if sorted(result.values())!=list(range(len(result))): raise ValueError(f"Invalid row mapping in {path}")
    return result


class Graph:
    def __init__(self, root):
        manifest=json.loads(Path(__file__).with_name("release.json").read_text())
        for name,expected in manifest.items():
            digest=hashlib.sha256()
            with (root/name).open("rb") as f:
                for chunk in iter(lambda:f.read(1<<20),b""): digest.update(chunk)
            if digest.hexdigest()!=expected: raise ValueError(f"Frozen DRKG file checksum mismatch: {name}")
        self.entities=mapping(root/FILES[2])
        self.relations=mapping(root/FILES[3])
        self.names=sorted(self.entities,key=self.entities.get)
        self.E,self.R=[np.load(root/f,mmap_mode="r",allow_pickle=False) for f in FILES[4:]]
        if self.E.shape!=(len(self.entities),400) or self.R.shape!=(len(self.relations),400):
            raise ValueError("Index and pretrained matrix shapes disagree")
        if not all(np.isfinite(m).all() for m in (self.E,self.R)): raise ValueError("Nonfinite embedding")
        with (root/FILES[1]).open() as f:
            self.gloss={r["Relation-name"]:r for r in csv.DictReader(f,delimiter="\t")}
        if self.relations.keys()!=self.gloss.keys(): raise ValueError("Incomplete relation glossary")
        self.types={}; buffers={r:array("i") for r in self.relations}
        for r,g in self.gloss.items():
            pair=tuple(r.split(":")[-2:])
            gloss=g["Connected entity-types"].replace("ATC","Atc").replace("Diisease","Disease")
            if sorted(pair)!=sorted(gloss.split(":")): raise ValueError(f"Glossary type mismatch: {r}")
            self.types[r]=pair
        # Validate actual ordered triples against relation suffix; glossary pair order
        # is descriptive and frequently reversed. Never auto-reverse a bad edge.
        types=[n.partition("::")[0] for n in self.names]
        self.quarantined={}
        self.triples=0
        with (root/FILES[0]).open() as f:
            for line in f:
                h,r,t=line.rstrip("\r\n").split("\t")
                i,j=self.entities[h],self.entities[t]
                self.triples+=1
                if (types[i],types[j])!=self.types[r]:
                    self.quarantined[r]=self.quarantined.get(r,0)+1
                    continue
                buffers[r].extend((i,j))
        self.edges={r:np.frombuffer(v,dtype=np.int32).reshape(-1,2) for r,v in buffers.items()}
        for v in self.edges.values(): v.flags.writeable=False

    @lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
    def walk(self,node,relation,forward):
        if node not in self.entities or relation not in self.edges: return []
        source,dest=(0,1) if forward else (1,0)
        if node.split("::")[0]!=self.types[relation][source]: raise ValueError(f"Invalid step {node} {relation}")
        pairs=self.edges[relation]
        return [self.names[i] for i in pairs[pairs[:,source]==self.entities[node],dest]]

You are the SCENE fork. Build the stage-3 DRKG visualization: Overseer-style 3D embedding cloud, but far more polished, with a live animated traversal of BOTH real graph edges and TransE embedding arithmetic. - `points.bin`: LE Float32, 3·97,238, entity-row order; PCA-3 coords, 98th-pct radius = 10. `types.bin`: Uint8 per entity → index into `scene.types`. `names.json`: `{ "<row>": label }` (hover only, lazy-load it).

# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

  query: Vec3
  targetEdges: number
  alsEdge: string | null
}

export type DrkgMatch = {
  rank: number
  id: string
  row: number
  name: string
  pos: Vec3
  /** True 400-d L2 from the profile's query. */
  distance: number
  viaGene: string
  directEdge: boolean
}

export type DrkgProfile = {
  lane: number
  name: string
  genes: DrkgGene[]
  unresolved: string[]
  matches: DrkgMatch[]
  edges: { from: number; to: number; rel: string }[]
}

export type DrkgScene = {
  meta: {
    model: string
    entities: number
    projection: string
    /** null for the clustered (non-linear) layout */
    explainedVariance: number[] | null
    relation: string
    formula: string
    universe: number
    topK: number
    /** Graph degree summary; present once `degree.bin` is written. */
    degree?: { min: number; median: number; p99: number; max: number }
  }
  types: { name: string; count: number }[]
  /** Optional: written once the layout is clustered; `clusters.bin` indexes into it. */
  clusters?: { id: number; label: string; size: number; dominantType: string; color?: string }[]
  als: { id: string; row: number; pos: Vec3; label: string }
  profiles: DrkgProfile[]
  handWritten: { drug: string; lane: number; source: string; id: string | null; rank: number | null; distance: number | null }[]
}

export type DrkgData = { scene: DrkgScene; positions: Float32Array; types: Uint8Array; clusters: Uint8Array | null; degree: Uint32Array | null }

/** A run is a folder: `scene.json` plus the binaries written beside it. Point `src` at a live backend's run. */
export const DEFAULT_SRC = '/drkg/scene.json'

const dirOf = (src: string) => src.slice(0, src.lastIndexOf('/') + 1)

async function get(url: string) {
  const res = await fetch(url)
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`${url}: ${res.status}`)
  return res
}

const runs = new Map<string, Promise<DrkgData>>()
const nameCache = new Map<string, Promise<Record<string, string>>>()

export function loadDrkg(src = DEFAULT_SRC) {
  let run = runs.get(src)
  if (run) return run
  const base = dirOf(src)
  run = Promise.all([
    get(src).then((r) => r.json() as Promise<DrkgScene>),
    get(base + 'points.bin').then((r) => r.arrayBuffer()),
    get(base + 'types.bin').then((r) => r.arrayBuffer()),
    get(base + 'clusters.bin').then((r) => r.arrayBuffer(), () => null),
    get(base + 'degree.bin').then((r) => r.arrayBuffer(), () => null),
  ]).then(([scene, p, t, c, d]) => ({
    scene,
    positions: new Float32Array(p),
    types: new Uint8Array(t),
    // Vite's dev server answers a missing file with index.html, so check the length too.
    clusters: c && c.byteLength === t.byteLength && scene.clusters ? new Uint8Array(c) : null,
    degree: d && d.byteLength === t.byteLength * 4 && scene.meta.degree ? new Uint32Array(d) : null,
  }))
  runs.set(src, run)
  run.catch(() => runs.delete(src)) // let a later mount retry
  return run
}

/** Hover labels for every entity; ~1 MB, so only fetched on first hover. */
export function loadNames(src = DEFAULT_SRC) {
  let names = nameCache.get(src)
  if (!names) {
    names = get(dirOf(src) + 'names.json').then((r) => r.json())
    nameCache.set(src, names)
    names.catch(() => nameCache.delete(src))
  }
  return names
}

export function useDrkg(src = DEFAULT_SRC) {
  const [state, setState] = useState<{ data: DrkgData | null; error: string | null }>({ data: null, error: null })
  useEffect(() => {
    let live = true
    loadDrkg(src).then(
      (data) => live && setState({ data, error: null }),
      (e: Error) => live && setState({ data: null, error: e.message }),
    )
    return () => {
      live = false
    }
  }, [src])
  return state
}

content.text:
The data passed an independent check. Two separate decoders, one of them running the browser's own decoding code, agree on every sampled entity. Edges and relation counts match the raw triples for all 97,238 entities, and embedding neighbours match a brute-force recompute.

The checker found three issues, which the workflow's fix pass will handle:
- **Edge priority used the wrong sources.** Three source names (Hetionet, IntAct and one other) are spelled differently in DRKG's relation list. They fell to the bottom of the ranking that decides which neighbours make the 44-edge cap, so curated edges lost to text-mining ones.
- **306 genes would get dead links.** Their IDs have no NCBI page.
- **Typing "als" doesn't find ALS.** Gene names starting with "ALS" outrank the disease, whose label is "Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis". This is the search a judge is most likely to type.

The browser test and design review are still running, then the fix pass. Once that finishes I'll test it myself, open the PR and merge.
